# crimesafe.uk

> UK crime statistics, safety scores, and neighbourhood crime data for England, Wales, and Northern Ireland — sourced from official UK Police open data.

## About
CrimeSafe UK provides UK crime statistics, safety scores, and neighbourhood crime data. Search by city, postcode, or street to find crime rates and safety information across England and Wales.

## Features / Content
- City pages: crime rates and average safety scores for major UK cities.
- Postcode & street search: look up crime data by postcode outcode and by street.
- Neighbourhood pages: per-neighbourhood crime breakdowns and safety scores.
- Police force pages: crime data grouped by the 44 UK police forces.
- Comparisons: head-to-head safety and crime comparisons between any two neighbourhoods.
- District / local-authority pages: crime overviews for UK districts.
- Most-dangerous rankings: highest- and safest-crime-area rankings across the UK.
- Embeddable widgets: lightweight "safety score" badges for any covered area.
- Blog: explainer articles on UK crime statistics, safest places to live, and how to check crime in your area.
- Maps: interactive crime maps (Leaflet-based).

## Key Facts
- 44 UK police forces covered.
- 4,929 neighbourhoods.
- 14 official crime categories tracked (violent crime, robbery, burglary, vehicle crime, theft, anti-social behaviour, criminal damage & arson, drugs, public order, weapons possession, and more).
- 38 city pages.
- ~274,000 neighbourhood-vs-neighbourhood comparison pages.
- 79 district pages.
- ~4,749 embeddable widget pages.
- ~4,060 postcode pages and ~489 street pages.
- Coverage: England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (Scotland excluded — different police data systems).
- Crime data is monthly; latest data April 2026.

- [Homepage](https://crimesafe.uk/): search and compare neighbourhoods, forces, and postcodes.
- [Cities](https://crimesafe.uk/city/): city-level crime rates and safety scores.
- [Districts](https://crimesafe.uk/districts/): UK district / local-authority crime overviews.
- [Forces](https://crimesafe.uk/forces/): the 44 UK police forces.
- [Rankings](https://crimesafe.uk/safest/): safest-area rankings.
- [Most Dangerous Areas](https://crimesafe.uk/dangerous/): highest-crime areas in the UK.
- [Blog](https://crimesafe.uk/blog/): crime and safety explainer articles.

- [FAQ](https://crimesafe.uk/faq/): common questions.
- Sample city: [Birmingham](https://crimesafe.uk/city/birmingham/).
- Sample comparison: [Abbey Hey vs Abram](https://crimesafe.uk/compare/abbey-hey-vs-abram/).

## URL Patterns
- City: `https://crimesafe.uk/city/<slug>/`
- Comparison: `https://crimesafe.uk/compare/<area-a>-vs-<area-b>/`
- District: `https://crimesafe.uk/district/<slug>/`
- Police force: `https://crimesafe.uk/forces/<slug>/`
- Postcode: `https://crimesafe.uk/postcode/<outcode>/`
- Street: `https://crimesafe.uk/streets/<slug>/`
- Embeddable widget: `https://crimesafe.uk/embed/<slug>/`
- Blog post: `https://crimesafe.uk/blog/<slug>/`

## Data Sources / Methodology
- All crime data comes from [data.police.uk](https://data.police.uk), the official UK Police open data portal, updated monthly by all 44 police forces.
- Safety scores (0–100) are calculated from per-capita crime rates adjusted for population size, so busy city centres and quiet residential areas can be compared fairly. Scores are percentile-based: a score of 80 means the area is safer than 80% of UK neighbourhoods.
- Update cadence: a weekly check (`check_new_data.py`) polls the data.police.uk `crime-last-updated` endpoint and flags when a newer monthly dataset is available; data is refreshed when new monthly releases land.
- Crime locations are anonymised by the police to protect victims, and figures represent reported crimes only.

## Notes
- This is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages.
- Not affiliated with any UK police force, the Home Office, or the government.
- For informational purposes only; actual crime levels may vary from reported figures.
- Scotland is not covered because Scottish police data uses different systems.
